articles.titleKo: 이라크, 첫 위성 지상국 개소
articles.summaryKo:
이라크 통신부 장관 무스타파 사나드가 바그다드에서 첫 위성 지상국을 개소하였다.
이 시설은 디지털 주권을 강화하고 통신 인프라를 발전시키기 위한 중요한 기초가 된다.
위성 지상국은 이라크의 국가 우주 프로그램의 초석 역할을 수행.
기술 그룹 Commercis와 협력하여 개발된 이 시설은 국내 광섬유 네트워크와 연결.
정부는 민간 기업과 보안 기관에 이 지역 게이트웨이로의 트래픽 이전을 촉구.
디지털 주권 강화를 위한 조치로 해석.
이 시설은 이라크의 지역 데이터 통로로서의 비전을 지원.
이라크의 통신 인프라 발전이 건설 및 투자 사업에 긍정적 영향을 미칠 가능성.
articles.description: Iraqi Minister of Communications Mustafa Sanad inaugurated on Sunday Iraq’s first satellite ground station in Baghdad. Iraqi Minister of Communications Mustafa Sanad and officials during the inauguration ceremony of Iraq’s first satellite station. Photo: Communication Ministry Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Minister of Communications Mustafa Sanad inaugurated on Sunday Iraq’s first satellite ground station in Baghdad, a step aiming to bolster digital sovereignty and develop the country’s telecommunications infrastructure. In a speech he delivered during the inauguration ceremony, Sanad said that Iraq’s acquisition of a satellite would be impossible without a ground station. The new facility will serve as a cornerstone for the country’s upcoming national space program, with future expansions planned to establish additional ground stations across other Iraqi provinces depending on population density and administrative assessment. The station also acts as a complete technological hub that includes a satellite communication gateway, a localized data center, and an internet exchange point. Developed in partnership with the technology group Commercis, the station links incoming satellite communications directly into Iraq’s expanding domestic fiber-optic terrestrial network. Iraq previously relied on international infrastructure located outside its borders to route satellite traffic. The government is now actively urging ministries, private companies, and security agencies to migrate their traffic to this local gateway to secure sensitive data. The station is part of a broader economic vision to transform Iraq into a regional data corridor. By leveraging its geographic location, Iraq aims to serve as a high-speed data transit bridge connecting networks across Asia, Africa, and Europe. The station provides high-speed enterprise internet, secure government communications, live television feeds, and commercial satellite broadcasting.

articles.description: KRG Deputy Minister of Natural Resources Ahmed Mufti outlines an energy roadmap, citing $10B in annual waste and urging a dedicated gas licensing round. Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq requires approximately eight billion standard cubic feet per day (scfd) of natural gas to achieve uninterrupted, 24-hour national electricity generation, according to Ahmed Mufti, Deputy Minister of Natural Resources in the Kurdistan Regional Government (KRG). In an analytical op-ed reviewed by the Iraqi News Agency (INA) on Sunday, October 18, 2026, Mufti highlighted that structural inefficiencies and energy waste cost the federal treasury roughly $10 billion annually, urging Baghdad and Erbil to launch a specialized gas licensing round and redirect industrial subsidies toward core infrastructure and upstream extraction. The KRG energy official pointed out that state-funded fuel subsidies for heavy industries—predominantly cement and steel plants—absorb nearly $8 billion annually. While commending the federal cabinet’s revised pricing mechanism for heavy fuel oil (black oil), which reduced subsidies to sell fuel to industrial plants at $400 per ton against an international benchmark of $650, Mufti emphasized that realized fiscal savings should be channeled directly into natural gas transmission networks. Transitioning heavy industry clusters, such as those in Sulaymaniyah’s Bazian district consuming 3,000 tons of fuel oil daily, to natural gas would significantly lower production costs, curb emissions, and free up heavy crude volumes for high-value export markets. Mufti outlined substantial upstream potential across key underdeveloped non-associated gas assets, including Akkas in Anbar and Mansuriya and Khashm Al-Ahmar in Diyala, calling for an investment licensing round backed by robust legal, security, and sovereign payment guarantees. Highlighting the Kurdistan Region’s foreign-investment model, he noted that output from the Khor Mor gas field surged from 350 million scfd in 2020 to 750 million scfd today, pushing aggregate regional gas production close to one billion scfd. Further development of adjacent fields—such as Chamchamal, Kurdamir, and Topkhana—could elevate regional production to between two and three billion scfd. To bridge supply shortages, Mufti proposed an integrated “gas-to-power” framework, where gas-fired generation in the north feeds directly into the federal transmission grid, cementing economic alignment between Baghdad and Erbil. Photo: Lauren Burke/AP Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Finance Minister Faleh Sari and World Bank Group Vice President for the Middle East and North Africa Ousmane Dione discussed on Thursday financing strategic projects and support for economic reforms in Iraq. The meeting took place on the sidelines of the annual meetings of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank Group, held in Bangkok, Thailand, according to a statement released by the Finance Ministry. Sari stressed the World Bank’s role in Iraq’s economic and financial transformation. He outlined the country’s desire to use the World Bank’s expertise and financial contributions to carry out significant projects in the energy, education, transportation, and digital transformation sectors. The step aims to promote sustainable development and improve the efficiency of public services in Iraq, according to Sari. Dione praised the collaboration with the Iraqi Finance Ministry, indicating that it has efficiently arranged its operational and communication mechanisms with the World Bank. The World Bank official highlighted that the efforts of the Iraqi government pave the way for additional initiatives to support the country’s economic and financial goals in the upcoming period. Sari reaffirmed last week Iraq’s commitment to continuing economic and financial reforms, diversifying revenue sources, and strengthening the role of the private sector. According to Sari, these measures aim to bolster economic stability and enhance the country’s capacity to deal with regional challenges. Sari noted that the government is addressing the economic consequences of the crisis in the Strait of Hormuz by reprioritizing expenditures, increasing non-oil revenues, and maintaining the state’s essential obligations while pursuing structural reforms. “Iraq Vision 2050” represents a strategic plan for reducing dependency on oil, broadening production, empowering the private sector, and achieving inclusive and sustainable economic growth, according to Sari. The minister noted that the reform package includes enhancing public financial management, automating customs and tax operations, boosting the business and investment climate, upgrading the banking sector, and increasing electronic payment systems. According to Sari, the partnership with the IMF and the World Bank Group supports the economic and financial reform program.
